title: Documents and KYC
blurb: Why a bank asks for ID, what to carry, and how students under 18 can still have an account.
t1.title: Why does the bank ask for ID?
t1.hook: Meena walks into a bank to open her first account. The clerk asks to see her ID. "But I only want to save!" she says.
t1.define: **KYC** means "Know Your Customer". The bank checks who you are and where you live before it opens your account.
t1.analogy: It is like a library card. The librarian notes your name and address, so the books go to the right person.
q1.prompt: Why does a bank ask for ID before opening an account?
q1.hint: Think about whose money it is.
q1.explain: The bank must know who owns the account. This also helps stop others from misusing it.
q1.opt.a: To know who owns the account
q2.prompt: What does the short form KYC stand for?
q2.explain: KYC stands for Know Your Customer.
t2.title: What to carry
t2.define: Most banks need proof of who you are and proof of where you live. Both must show your name.
t2.steps.1: One ID proof with your name and photo, such as a government ID card.
t2.steps.2: One address proof, such as an electricity bill or a rent agreement.
t2.steps.4: One filled form, which the bank gives you.
q3.prompt: Count one ID proof, one address proof, the passport photos and the form. How many items is that in all? Type a number.
q3.hint: Add up every item in the list. Count each photo.
q3.explain: One ID plus one address proof plus {photos} photos plus one form is {docsTotal} items.
q4.prompt: Which of these is a good address proof?
q4.hint: It must show your name and where you live.
q4.explain: A bill or agreement with your name and address proves where you live.
q4.opt.a: A recent electricity bill with your name and address
t3.title: Accounts for students under 18
t3.define: A **minor account** is for someone under 18. A parent or guardian signs with the child. The child can use it as the bank allows.
t3.mistake: Many students think they cannot have an account until they are 18. Banks do offer accounts for minors, with a parent or guardian.
q5.prompt: Asha is {minorAge}. She will be {adultAge} soon. How many years until then? Type a number.
q6.prompt: Ravi is 16 and wants to save his pocket money. What is true?
q6.hint: Read the card about minor accounts.
q6.explain: He can have a minor account, opened with a parent or guardian.
q6.opt.a: He can open a minor account with a guardian
q6.opt.b: He must wait until he is 18
q6.fb.b: Age under 18 does not shut the door. Minor accounts exist, with a parent or guardian.
q6.opt.c: He cannot ever have an account
t4.title: Lab: the nominee
t4.define: A **nominee** is the person you name to receive the money in your account if you die. Naming one saves your family much trouble.
t4.explore: Open the lab. Change the balance and the number of nominees to see each share.
q7.prompt: In the lab, set the money to {labBal} and the nominees to {labNom}. How much does each nominee receive? Type a number in rupees.
q7.hint: Divide the money by the number of nominees.
q8.prompt: Asha names her mother as nominee. While Asha is alive, what can her mother do with the account?
q8.hint: A nominee matters only after the account holder dies.
q8.explain: A nominee gets the money only after the account holder dies. Until then the account is only Asha's.
q8.opt.a: Nothing: the account is still only Asha's
q8.fb.b: A nominee is not a joint owner. A nominee is only named to receive the money later.
t5.title: Keeping your details current
t5.tradeoff: Giving documents takes a little time. In return, the bank can tell your money apart from everyone else's and reach you when needed.
t5.steps.1: If you move house, tell the bank your new address.
t5.steps.2: Give the bank a fresh address proof when it asks.
t5.steps.3: Keep your phone number the same, or update it at the bank.
q9.prompt: Meena moves to a new town. What should she do about her bank account?
q9.hint: The bank has her old address.
q9.explain: She should tell the bank her new address and give proof when asked, so her KYC stays current.
q9.opt.a: Update her address with the bank
q9.opt.b: Do nothing and hope for the best
q10.prompt: {friends} friends each open an account. Each needs {photos} photos. How many photos in all? Type a number.
q10.hint: Multiply the friends by the photos each.
glossary.bank_kyc.def: Know Your Customer: the bank checks who you are and where you live.
glossary.bank_nominee.def: The person you name to receive your account money after you die.
glossary.bank_minor_account.def: An account for someone under 18, opened with a parent or guardian.
